o1.biggest_strength: Translates the data directly into smart operational gating (like tying the staged rollout to daily ticket limits) and delivers exceptional, brand-perfect launch copy.
o1.biggest_mistake: Inviting power users to beta test on November 23 only leaves one week to fix complex migration bugs before the December 1 code freeze.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Moving the power-user beta test earlier in November to give engineering a bigger buffer before the code freeze (though it is already a 10).

o2.biggest_strength: The inclusion of specific, numerical success metrics and a pre-planned 'Plan B' to pause the rollout if support gets overwhelmed.
o2.biggest_mistake: The X launch post is only a single tweet, which is too brief for a major version launch and misses the chance to fully showcase the features.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Expanding the X post into a multi-tweet thread that highlights each new feature with its own short screen recording.

reason: Both are phenomenal, data-driven plans that perfectly diagnose the retention signals and support risks. Output 1 wins because its launch copy is much stronger—particularly the multi-post X thread that perfectly executes the brand voice and video principles.
